meaningMnemonic: A single horizontal stroke. One line, one finger held up, one of anything. The simplest possible mark means the simplest possible number.
Two legs and nothing above them, planted apart and ready to run. Just the legs, no body attached.
Like Person, but the strokes cross over at the top, as if someone is ducking their head to get through a low doorway. You have to stoop to enter.
Two strokes splitting apart, opening outward. Eight is the number that divides and divides again: eight into four, four into two.
Two walls and a roof with no floor and no door, a wide open frame you could drive a truck through.
A flat sheet draped over something, edges hanging down on both sides. A cloth thrown over the furniture.
Two small strokes leaning together, like the first two icicles forming under a gutter. Water is three strokes, ice is only two, because the cold froze one off.
A flat surface with two legs beneath it. Look at it side-on and it is unmistakably a small table.
An open box seen from the side: walls on the left and right, a floor at the bottom, nothing on top. Drop something in.
A blade with a handle curving off to one side, hanging point-down. A butcher knife on the wall.
An arm flexed hard, elbow bent and bicep bulging. Pure muscle, pure power.
An arm curling around from above to enclose something, the way you wrap your arm around a package to carry it.
A small scoop with a handle, tilted as if lifting something out of a bowl. A spoon halfway to your mouth.
Three sides of a box with the right side missing, lying open on its side so you can slide things in.
A single flick of the brush, like a drop of ink flung onto the page. Not a line, not a shape, just a dot.
A bent hook, like the number 2 written in a hurry. Second place gets the crooked trophy.
A vertical line with a hook curling off the bottom, exactly like a fishing hook hanging in the water.
Two horizontal strokes stacked up. One line was one, so two lines is two. Counting could not be more literal.
A flat top with a little handle poking up, sitting over whatever comes below. A lid on a pot.
Two legs mid-stride, a body walking away from you. The whole person, reduced to their walk.
A cross, one stroke over another. Ten fingers, two hands crossed over each other. Also the Roman numeral X turned upright.
A crack in a heated turtle shell. Ancient diviners burned bones and read the cracks that split across them to tell the future.
A kneeling figure bent at the knee, seen from the side. This is the shape of someone pressed down, the way a stamped seal presses into wax.
A flat top with one long stroke falling away down the left. A cliff face, seen side on, with the overhang above you.
A small closed curl, wrapped in on itself, keeping whatever is inside to itself. Nothing gets out. Private.
A right hand with the fingers simplified to strokes. A hand reaching out to take something one more time. Again.
A simple open square: an open mouth seen straight on. This is one of the most literal pictures in the whole system.
The same square as Mouth, but drawn larger and fully closed with nothing inside. A wall around a space. Nothing gets in or out.
A cross planted on a baseline: a seedling pushing up out of the ground. The bottom stroke is the widest, because that is the ground itself.
Almost identical to Earth, but here the TOP stroke is the widest. The scholar stands with their broad shoulders up top, head high, not rooted in the dirt.
A leg mid-step with the foot trailing behind, the shape of walking away. Movement leaving the frame.
A crescent moon, half drawn, just beginning to show. Not yet full night, only evening.
A person standing with arms flung wide and legs apart, showing you how big something was. The fisherman gesture.
A figure kneeling with legs folded and arms crossed in the lap, the traditional seated posture. Curved and low to the ground.
A baby wrapped in swaddling: a big round head on top, arms out to the sides, and the legs bundled together into one stroke below.
A roof with a chimney on top and eaves hanging down both sides. Anything under this radical happens indoors.
A hand with a mark just below the wrist, showing where the pulse is. That distance, hand to pulse point, was the old measure. One inch.
One tiny stroke in the middle with two even tinier flecks either side, as if something has been chipped down to almost nothing.
Like Big, a standing person, but one stroke is bent and pushed out of line. The figure cannot stand straight. Lame.
A body lying flat with the legs drawn up, seen from the side. The shape of someone collapsed and not getting up.
A single shoot pushing up out of the ground with two small leaves opening off the stem. The very first growth.
Three peaks rising off a flat base, the tallest in the middle. A mountain range drawn by a child, and by ancient China.
Three flowing lines running in parallel down the page. Water moving in a channel. River.
An I-beam, or the ruler a carpenter carries: a flat top, a flat bottom, and a solid upright joining them. A tool for building. Work.
A thread coiling back on itself, doubling around to point at where it started. It always comes back to me. Self.
A hanging towel: a bar across the top, and the fabric falling down from it in folds. Cloth on a rail.
A forked pole with a crossbar, the tool used to beat and hang things out. Whatever is hung on it ends up dry.
A tiny twist of silk, so small it is barely there. A single short thread pulled loose from the weave.
The Cliff radical with a dot added on top. That dot is a roof: someone has built a lean-to shelter against the cliff face.
An exaggerated version of Step, stretched out at the bottom. The leg is extended as far as it will go. A long stride.
Two hands coming up from below, palms open, joining together to lift or offer something.
A shaft with a barb hooking off it, and a cord for retrieval. A thrown weapon you can pull back. Javelin.
The curve of a bow with the string slack, seen from the side. Two bends and a taut line.
A blunt animal snout in profile, or a hand with the fingers pointing sideways. Three horizontal lines with a spine down one edge.
Three short strokes swept in the same direction, like hair, fur, or the strokes of a brush. Always something with texture.
A leg taking a short pace, with the knee bent. This radical almost always means going somewhere, one step at a time.
An organ with the chambers drawn as three dots and the muscle as the sweeping stroke beneath. The literal shape of a heart, not the valentine.
A long pole with a blade jutting off the side and a tassel at the top. A weapon for hooking and slashing, not stabbing.
A single door panel on its hinge, hanging in a frame. One panel only, because a double door is a different character.
A hand with the fingers spread and the wrist below: three fingers as horizontal strokes, the thumb sweeping off, and the arm running down.
A hand reaching up to take hold of a limb: the cross at the top is the branch, the strokes below are the arm pulling it down.
Branch, but with a hand raised behind it holding a stick. Not taking the branch, hitting with it. A sharp rap.
A figure with a decorated chest, marked with the crossing lines of a tattoo. The oldest writing was cut into skin and shell. Script.
A long handle with two marks near the top, the ladle used to scoop grain or wine out of a barrel. Also the shape of the constellation.
An axe head on a short handle, blade angled down toward the block. Heavy at the top, exactly where the weight of an axe sits.
A plough with the blade cutting sideways, the tool that carved fields into square lots. Direction and shape at once.
A box with one line through the middle: the sun with a mark at its centre, as ancient astronomers drew the sunspot. This one is everywhere, so fix it now.
The same box as Sun, but stretched tall and cut open on one side, with two lines inside. A crescent, leaning. Tall and open means night.
A trunk running down the middle, branches out to each side, and roots splaying at the bottom. The whole tree in four strokes.
A person on their knees with their mouth wide open, head thrown back. Yawning, gasping, wanting. Something is missing.
A footprint pressed into the ground: toes at the top, heel below. The foot has come down and stayed there. Stop.
Bare bones left after the flesh is gone, cracked and splayed. The most direct way the old script drew death.
A hand at the bottom gripping a shaft with a heavy head. Not a blade, a bludgeon. Something you swing.
The Woman radical with a bar struck through her. This is a prohibition sign, and it means exactly what a line through anything means. Do not.
Two Spoon radicals set side by side, facing the same way. Two identical things placed together so you can hold them up against each other.
A tail or a tuft of hair, with the strands sweeping off in the same direction and curling at the tip.
A hand holding up a banner on a pole. The standard a family marched under, the mark of who your people were. Clan.
Wisps rising and curling as they lift off something hot. Three strokes drifting upward and bending in the air.
A central current with spray flicking off both sides. When it shrinks to the left of a kanji it becomes three droplets, but this full form is a whole river.
A central flame with sparks flying off both sides, wider at the bottom where it burns hottest. Compare Water: same idea, opposite element.
A sprout pushing up through the soil line, already sending out its first leaf. Growth breaking through. Life.
A wooden pail with slats and a handle, a plain object made to be picked up and used for something.
A plot of farmland seen from above, divided into four quarters by the paths running between them. Rice fields, mapped.
A length of fabric hanging with the loose end trailing at the bottom. A whole bolt, not a scrap.
Two feet pointing away from each other, mid-stride, the trace left by someone climbing. Footsteps going up.
The Sun radical with a single ray shooting off the top. Not the sun itself, but the glare coming off it. Blinding white.
A hand pulling a hide off an animal, the sheet peeling away below. Skin being taken as a whole piece.
A shallow bowl on a footed stand, seen from the side. The flat base underneath is what tells you it is set down on a table.
A hand reaching down from above, fingers curled to grab. Every time you see it, something is being seized from overhead.
A hand holding an axe, raised and ready to work. The one who went out and did the hard labour for the household.
The left half of a log after it has been split down the middle. Jagged on one edge, flat on the other.
The right half of that same split log, mirrored. Two halves, two radicals: this is the piece that fell the other way.
Interlocking teeth seen from the side, hooked and overlapping. Not a full mouth, just the part that bites.
A horned head seen head on: the crossbar is the horns, the line down the middle is the face. One horn is cut short, which is what separates it from the Noon radical.
The Big radical with a small mark added at the shoulder. A person with a dog sitting at their side, that little dot being the animal itself.
A thread disappearing under a cover, going somewhere you cannot see. Dark, deep, and not fully knowable. Profound.
Three discs strung on a cord, with a single dot marking the flaw in the stone. Remove the dot and it becomes King, so the dot is the whole difference.
A vine curling on both sides with the fruit hanging heavy in the middle. You can see the weight pulling the stem down.
Two roof tiles hooked over one another, the way they interlock along a roofline so the rain runs off.
A mouth with something held inside it, marked by the line across the middle. Whatever is being savoured, it is worth keeping in there. Sweet.
An eye stood on its end: the outer box is the lid, the two lines inside are the iris and pupil. Turned upright to fit the square, but still an eye.
A shaft with a hook and a tassel hanging off it. Compare Arrow: the spear is the one with the decoration, because you keep hold of it.
A shaft with the flights at the top and the point driving down. Plainer than the spear, because you only get to use it once.
A boulder sitting at the foot of a cliff. The Cliff radical up top, and the rock that fell off it below.
An altar table with offerings laid on it and something dripping down. Whatever this radical touches has to do with gods and ritual.
The Tree radical with a heavy head drooping off the top. That droop is the whole difference: grain bends under its own ripeness, a tree does not.
A roof with an opening split beneath it. A hole dug into the hillside and covered over. Cave.
A person planted on a baseline, arms out and feet apart. The bottom stroke is the ground, which is what makes this standing rather than just being.
Two stalks side by side, each with leaves hanging off the joint. Bamboo always comes in a stand, never alone.
Grains scattered from a central point, flying off in all four directions. What a dropped handful looks like on the floor.
A skein of silk twisted at the top with the loose ends trailing below. Fine strands, bundled.
A clay pot with a lid on top and a wide belly below. Made to hold something and be sealed.
A head seen from the front: curled horns sweeping out at the top, face below. The horns are what make it a sheep and not a cow.
Two wings side by side, each with the barbs marked inside. Not one feather, a pair beating.
A bent figure leaning on a stick, hair straggling above. Age drawn as posture.
A beard hanging from a chin, strands falling straight down. It came to mean a connector, the way a beard connects to the face.
A wooden blade with a handle and the tines biting into the soil. A tool dragged through earth.
An ear in profile, with the outer rim and the folds inside it. Long and vertical, the way an ear actually sits on the head.
A hand gripping a brush upright, the bristles running down below the fist. This is the radical of writing itself.

Ribs of flesh with the striations marked inside. It looks almost identical to Moon when squeezed to the left of a kanji, so watch for it: on the left it is usually meat, and the character is usually about the body.
An eye turned on its side and staring downward, the way a servant lowers their gaze in front of the king. Watching, but never meeting the eye.
A nose, drawn front-on with the bridge and nostrils. Japanese speakers point at their own nose to mean me, which is exactly how this came to mean self.
An arrow that has landed and stuck in the ground, the flat line at the bottom being the earth it hit. The journey is over. Arrive.
A stone bowl seen in cross-section, with grain inside waiting to be pounded. Hollow, heavy, and open at the top.
A tongue sticking out of a mouth, the Mouth radical below and the tongue thrust up out of it.
Two feet pointing in opposite directions, pulling against each other. Nothing moves when both legs want to go elsewhere.
A hull with a deck line across it and cargo marked inside, seen from the side. Two dots for whatever it is carrying.
An eye that has stopped moving and fixed on something, refusing to turn away. A hard, unmoving stare.
A person bent over another, from the older sense of complexion and passion. The face, and what shows in it.
The striped head and shoulders of a big cat, crouched over the top of whatever it is about to land on. It always sits above.
A grub or worm with a swollen body and a small head, curled at the tail. The old script used it for anything crawling, snakes included.
The Dish radical with a drop falling into it. A bowl catching what comes out of the sacrifice.
A crossroads seen from above, two paths meeting and running off in four directions. Characters using it wrap around whatever is in the middle.
A robe seen from the front: the collar at the top and the sleeves and hem falling away below.
A bird settling into its nest, which is what birds do at sundown. The sun sets in the west, so the bird going home points the direction.
The Eye radical set on top of a pair of legs. An eye that walks around: not just an eye, but someone actively looking. See.
A horn with the ridges marked along it, tapering to the point. Curved at the top where it leaves the skull.
A mouth at the bottom with lines rising out of it, sound coming out in waves. The lid on top is the tongue moving.
A gap opening between two slopes with a mouth at the bottom. The ground splits and the valley floor lies between.
A stemmed serving vessel with a lid, which is what the character originally drew. It came to mean bean because that is what got served in it.
A pig seen from the side: the snout up top, the spine running down, and the legs and curled tail sticking out below.
A long-bodied animal arched to pounce, back curved and legs tucked. Any clawed beast that hunts low to the ground.
A cowrie shell with the ridges marked and the two feet of the creature poking out below. Shells were currency, so this radical marks money almost every time you see it.
Earth over fire. Soil scorched by flame until it glows. Red.
Earth on top and a foot below, driving off the ground. The ground is under you and you are pushing off it. Run.
A knee at the top and the foot planted below it, the whole leg from the joint down. Compare Run, which is the same foot in motion.
A person in profile with a swollen belly, the shape used for a pregnant woman. The whole trunk, not a limb.
A wagon seen from above: the axle running vertically, the wheel bed in the middle, and the load-bars top and bottom.
A tattooing needle, the tool used to mark criminals. What it stood for was the punishment. Bitter, painful, hard to swallow.
A clam extending its foot from the shell, which farmers watched for as the sign to start the day. It marks time and season.
A narrow-necked jar with liquid inside, the vessel fermented drink was aged in. The line inside is what is settling at the bottom.
A hand picking a single grain out from the rest, separating one thing from many. Telling apart.
Field over Earth. Farmland and the soil beneath it, which together is what a village actually was.
Metal nuggets buried under a mound of earth, the two dots being the ore still in the ground. It covers all metals, not only gold.
Long hair streaming down from an old person, unbound and trailing. Length, and by extension age and seniority.
A pair of swinging doors facing each other, hinged on either side. Two panels, unlike the Door radical, which is only one.
A hand reaching down to seize a tail, catching something and holding it fast. Capture.
A bird in profile with the wing folded and the tail cropped short. Compare Bird, which is the same creature with a full tail and legs.
A sky with a cloud beneath it and four drops falling in the space below. This one is a straightforward picture, and always weather.
Growth on top and moon beneath: the colour of new plants under moonlight. Japanese uses this one word for both blue and green.
Two wings spread and beating in opposite directions. Nothing works when the halves are set against each other. Wrong.
A head with the outline of the face drawn around an eye at the centre. The surface of a person, not the skull.
A hide stretched on a frame, head at the top and tail below, pulled taut to dry.
Feet pacing around a stretched hide, walking it soft. Leather is the raw skin, this is the worked version.
The Speech radical with an extra line inside the mouth. Not words, just the noise itself. Sound.
A head on a pair of legs, from the older sense of a page or a face. When it sits on the right of a kanji, the character is usually about the head.
An insect inside an enclosure being blown along. The old belief was that wind carried creatures in it.
A bird with both wings raised and the body between them, caught at the top of the beat.
A lid over a heaped bowl of food. The lid is coming off and there is a mound underneath. Eat.
A face with the hair marked above it, the whole thing from the neck up. Compare Face, which is only the front.
Grain over Sun. Rice warming in the heat and giving off its smell.
A horse in profile: the mane flying up top, the body in the middle, and the four legs as strokes along the bottom.
A joint socket up top with flesh hanging below. The hard part and the meat still attached to it.
A watchtower with a roof, an upper storey and a lower one, stacked. Buildings are how height was drawn.
Long hair falling from a head, with the strands trailing off to the side. Always about hair.
A three-legged cooking pot with a lid, the vessel used over an open fire. Legs so the flames get underneath.
A figure with an oversized head wearing a mask, and a tail curling behind. Human-shaped, but not human.
A fish standing on its nose: head at the top, scaled body in the middle, and the tail fanned out at the bottom.
A bird with the crest on its head, the eye, the wing folded along the body, and the tail feathers spread below.
Antlers branching at the top with the body and legs beneath. The antlers are the whole giveaway.
A grain stalk with the roots showing beneath, drawn as something that arrived from elsewhere. Wheat came to China from the west.
Fibres hanging to dry under a lean-to. The Dotted Cliff radical for the shelter, and the plant stalks beneath it.
A field with light spreading through it, the colour of ripe crops seen across open ground.
Soot marks around a chimney flue with the fire below. What smoke leaves behind on everything it touches. Black.
A drum on a stand with a hand raised beside it holding the stick. The instrument and the striking, both in one character.
The Self radical, which is already a nose, with a breathing apparatus added below. When self stopped meaning nose, this took over the literal job.
Grain heads growing at exactly the same height across a field, trimmed level. Uniform, aligned. Even.
An open mouth with the teeth drawn in rows inside it. The stop mark on top gives the sound, the teeth below give the meaning.
A crowned head on the left and a scaled, writhing body on the right. Elaborate, because a dragon should be.
A turtle seen from above: head at the top, shell with its plate markings in the middle, feet out to the sides, and the tail below.
